insight: Created in the Stanford NLP group; the name stands for "Declarative Self-improving Python."
name: DSPy
tagline: Program — don't prompt — your language models.
description: DSPy is an open-source Python framework for building LLM applications by writing modular code instead of brittle prompt strings. You declare input/output signatures and compose modules, then DSPy compiles and optimizes the underlying prompts — and can even tune model weights — for classifiers, RAG pipelines, and agent loops.

modelSupport.notes: Provider-agnostic — works with any LLM backend you configure.

edge: Optimizes prompts (and even model weights) automatically from your data, instead of leaving you to hand-tune brittle prompt strings.
cons: Steeper learning curve than direct prompting
Optimizers can add compute and cost

references.title: DSPy: An open-source framework for LLM-powered applications
